name: Mktg.ai
summary: Always-on AI marketing analyst: unified creative visibility, live performance signals and plain-language questions over your own spend data — no public pricing, demo-first.
best_for: marketing teams with real media spend across channels who want an always-on AI analyst — unified creative visibility, live performance signals and plain-language questions over their own data. It layers on top of your existing platforms rather than replacing them, with the vendor putting real-time data in week one and full onboarding at two to three weeks
skip_if: your ad spend is modest (the value scales with budget waste, and yours is small), or you want transparent self-serve pricing before a sales call
honest_knock: The price is still hidden — a 404 where the pricing page should be, and no pricing item in the navigation — which for a tool that promises spend transparency is an irony worth noticing, and the FAQ makes it sharper: its own introduction says it covers what the platform costs, and then no answer in it names a figure. What the FAQ does publish is the tier names, Growth and Enterprise, and the fact that EU data residency is Enterprise-only. The ROI story is also the vendor's own: the homepage tile assumes a $5M budget and puts a 3% efficiency gain at $150K alongside $100K of reallocated spend, which is 2% of the same budget. Ask for verified case numbers at your spend level on the demo call.

pricing.notes: No public pricing (re-verified 25 September 2026): mktg.ai/pricing still returns 404 and the navigation carries no pricing item, so every route ends at 'Book a Demo'. The tiers themselves are no longer secret, though — the FAQ names Growth and Enterprise above the entry level and describes what they add (dedicated onboarding on both; a dedicated customer success manager, SLA-backed response times and quarterly business reviews on top of that). Email support is on every plan; custom integrations and EU data residency are Enterprise-only, with US data centres the default. The machine-readable llms.txt is Wix boilerplate advertising an MCP endpoint and carries no price either. Rates require a sales conversation.

cost_traps.label: Quote-only pricing
cost_traps.evidence: No public pricing: /pricing 404s and every route ends at 'Book a Demo' (re-verified 25 Sep 2026)
